text: 9 and results with imat- inib have challenged the role of HSCT as first-line therapy for chronic phase CML.1 While HSCT is still an option in suitable patients such as younger patients with HLA-iden- tical sibling donors,4,5 or those with high-risk disease and low transplantation risk,2 most recommend an initial peri- od of therapy with imatinib since the response can either reinforce or weaken the indication for HSCT.6,8,9 Ongoing advances in alternative donor sources (such as the use of HLA-matched unrelated donors and cord blood), im- proved HLA typing techniques, and less toxic non-myelo- ablative regimens are broadening the use of HSCT.1,5 Au- tologous HSCT has also been investigated, but no advantage over interferon-based regimens has been shown.8 Options in patients who relapse after HSCT in- clude the use of donor lymphocyte infusions, tyrosine ki- nase inhibitors, or interferon alfa.1,2 Although now no longer a first-line treatment, in most pa- tients, interferon alfa is associated with improved survival compared with busulfan or hydroxycarbamide,16 and the addition of low-dose cytarabine to interferon alfa im- proves response rates but increases toxicity compared with interferon alfa alone.17 Hydroxycarbamide is somewhat more effective, and better tolerated, than busulfan.18 Occasionally, patients present in advanced phase. Those in early blast crisis may be treated initially with imatinib or other tyrosine kinase inhibitors, and then proceed to allo- geneic HSCT.4,8 A longer trial of imatinib is possible for patients diagnosed in accelerated phase.8 For those who progress to advanced disease while on imatinib, options include dasatinib or nilotinib, HSCT, or investigational therapy.1 Investigational therapies for CML include omacetaxine mepesuccinate, farnesyl transferase inhibitors such as lonafarnib and tipifarnib, hypomethylating agents such as azacitidine and decitabine, histone deacetylase inhibitors, and vaccines.5,15 Combinations of imatinib with other drugs are also under investigation.2 1.
